content:
Jess (support): opening thread. Multiple EU customers reporting large p95/p99 regressions on /v1/generate starting around 2026-03-15 09:05 UTC. Symptoms: extra 200-400ms TLS handshake delay, intermittent 504s. Putting this into incidents channel.

Maya (SRE): ack. Any deploys in the window?

Jess (support): no deploys. Timeline from support shows onset ~09:05 UTC, broadside across eu-west and eu-north.

Alex (oncall): I'm on it. Pulling edge latency heatmap. Initial look: eu-west pop-5 spikes to p95 ~480ms. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/edges/heatmap?region=eu-west

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-1302 created and notified oncall.

Sam (netops): network telemetry: sudden increase in BGP AS-path length for prefixes served by pop-5 starting 09:03 UTC. Upstream AS reports an outage on one of their interfaces; traffic rerouted via a transit path through eu-central. Seen increased retransmits on pop-5.

Maya (SRE): can we get a customer traceroute + internal pop->origin traceroute to confirm cross-region detour? Also check DNS mappings for anycast VIPs.

Jess (support): customer traceroute (Zurich user):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (34.254.12.210), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.0 ms  0.8 ms  0.9 ms
 2  193.51.9.5  10.2 ms  10.1 ms  10.3 ms
 3  149.112.9.1  22.8 ms  22.6 ms  22.7 ms
 4  34.254.12.210  410.6 ms  412.1 ms  409.9 ms
```
big jump at the edge hop.

Sam (netops): internal pop-5 -> origin traceroute:
```
traceroute to origin-eu-west-02 (10.141.3.22)
 1  pop-5-router  0.9 ms  1.1 ms
 2  backbone-west  2.2 ms  2.1 ms
 3  transit-eu-central  206.4 ms  206.0 ms
 4  origin-eu-west-02  206.7 ms
```
shows detour via eu-central adding ~200ms.

Alex (oncall): that detour would explain the extra handshake RTT and the p99 blowup. Check TLS logs for handshake retransmits.

Maya (SRE): TLS summaries: increased TLS_SYN_RETRANSMIT and longer handshake durations on pop-5 in 09:02-09:12 window. Sample log: `TLS_HANDSHAKE_RETRY pop=pop-5 count=62 window=09:02-09:12`

Jess (support): support captured tcpdump from an affected client:
```
09:05:12.987654 IP client -> edge: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
09:05:13.188123 IP client -> edge: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, length 0  (retransmit)
09:05:13.389456 IP edge -> client: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 28960, length 0
```
shows SYN retransmit and delayed SYN-ACK.

Sam (netops): upstream confirmed a flapped interface causing route churn and longer AS-paths. Their mitigation at ~09:30 UTC fixed the transit path, but our pop-5 FIB still held stale next-hops until we refreshed.

Maya (SRE): Mitigation steps to apply now: 1) force FIB refresh on pop-5, 2) lower DNS TTL for eu anycast VIPs to accelerate client re-resolve, 3) temporarily steer away traffic from pop-5 while it stabilizes.

Alex (oncall): I'm executing the FIB refresh and applying steering. Running: `ssh pop-5 'vtysh -c "clear bgp *"'` and `sudo /sbin/ip route flush cache` where it's safe.

ops-bot: Action logged: FIB refresh requested by Alex.

Sam (netops): running controlled clears now. Monitoring route convergence.

Jess (support): support reports some customers improving already; p95 from 480ms -> 110-150ms for many users. A subset still sees spikes.

Maya (SRE): likely sequence: upstream interface flapped -> BGP path chosen via transit eu-central -> additional ~200ms path -> TCP/TLS handshake RTT increased -> retransmits -> client timeouts and p99 regression. Good that we cleared FIB.

Alex (oncall): I've pushed a temporary routing weight change in runtime to shift ~35% of new sessions away from pop-5 and lowered eu VIP TTL to 20s for affected zones. Also opened a customer advisory: "We identified transient routing issue at an upstream peer leading to elevated TLS handshake times for EU users; we've applied routing fixes and are monitoring."

Priya (peering): I'll follow up with the upstream for their full incident timeline and request improved dampening and BGP flap notifications. Opening peering ticket PEER-789.

Maya (SRE): Post-incident action items: - implement BGP-flap alert that triggers safe FIB refresh automation (INFRA-3302), - add per-pop TLS handshake retransmit metrics and alerting, - add a runbook for health-check-based automatic traffic steering thresholds.

Sam (netops): creating INFRA-3302 with proposed automation and safety locks (rate limit clears, manual override).

Alex (oncall): suggest adding a runtime policy: if pop p95 > 250ms for 5m, reduce new session traffic to that pop by 25% automatically. I'll draft the PR and a canary.

Jess (support): sending customer follow-ups and attaching tcpdump/traces to the ticket. Closing the support escalation as mitigated for now.

Maya (SRE): we'll compile a full postmortem once upstream provides their report; target a draft by EOD.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-1302 status changed to: monitoring.
